subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - FinSolve
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Larson <emma.larson@finsolve.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@finsolve.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - FinSolve

Thanks again for taking the time today, Emma and Rajiv — really appreciate the context on your roadmap. Wanted to capture our notes and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Summary of pain and goals
- Pain: Production inference spikes during end-of-month reporting causing latency >1.2s and occasional 429s when using shared endpoints.
- Goal: Predictable latency SLO of <=300ms P95 for interactive flows and stable throughput for bulk jobs (batch score runs).
- Constraint: Data isolation and strict audit/logging for regulatory audits (SOC2 + internal finance controls).

Current stack
- API layer: in-house Python FastAPI endpoints calling a managed LLM API (third-party) for prompt generation and scoring.
- Model needs: mix of retrieval-augmented generation for summaries + a reranker for candidate scoring (~6 candidate rerank calls per user event).
- Infra: Kubernetes on AWS (us-west-2), VPN to partner services.

Redwood Dedicated fit (initial assessment)
- Reserved GPU pools: Our Dedicated pools can provide isolated GPU capacity for FinSolve with pinned models/versions — addresses isolation and predictability.
- Throughput: Based on your estimate of 250 TPS peak across reranker calls (see below), we recommend a 2x safety buffer for predictable headroom.
- Autoscaling / burst: Dedicated supports configured surge capacity (burst) for monthly peaks; we can set autoscale triggers by queue length and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Compliance: Private control plane + KMS integrations and audit logs can meet your SOC2 evidence needs; we’ll surface the audit logs for your security team.

Clarifying numbers you shared (please confirm)
- Interactive flows: ~150 active users during peak window, ~6 reranker calls per user -> ~900 reranker calls/minute (~15 TPS) — please confirm if these are per-second or per-minute metrics.
- Batch jobs: nightly scoring of ~50k documents that require throughput for 2-3 hour window.

Success criteria for POC
- P95 latency <=300ms for interactive reranker calls under simulated peak traffic.
- No cross-tenant data exposure; separate GPU pool and audit logs verified.
- Cost projection within the target budget range we discussed (you mentioned $X–$Yk/mo - placeholder until procurement confirms).

Next steps
1) You confirm the TPS numbers and clarify whether counts are per-second or per-minute (Rajiv, can you confirm?).
2) Redwood to send a draft SOW + pricing estimate for a 6-week POC (attached draft SOW and pricing workbook).
3) Security: Rafael will follow up with a SOC2 artifact package and an ingestion guide for audit logs.
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra lead (propose next Tue 4/21 or Wed 4/22).

Attachments: Finsolve_POC_SOW_v1.pdf (draft), redwood-dedicated-capacity-pricing.xlsx (ballpark numbers).

Thanks 
Marissa Cole

From: Emma Larson <emma.larson@finsolve.com>

Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - FinSolve

Marissa — thanks for the recap, this looks great. Quick clarifications below.

Numbers
- The 900 reranker calls figure is per minute — my mistake in the call. Peak interactive TPS is closer to 15 TPS for rerankers.
- Nightly batch: yes, ~50k docs; typically we want that done within a 3-hour window, often starts at 02:00 local.

Compliance
- We will need the audit logs and proof of KMS integration for the SOW. Our procurement team needs the SOC2 Type II report and the list of sub-processors.

Procurement / budget
- We are targeting a POC budget of up to $30k for the initial 6 weeks (includes any reserved capacity and engineering support). Finance will require a short SOW and an invoice schedule.

Next steps (agree)
- Rajiv will confirm availability for the technical deep-dive (he’s copied).
- Please include the SOC2 artifacts and a sample audit log output in the follow-up.

Thanks,
Emma
Head of Platform Engineering
FinSolve
emma.larson@finsolve.com
